query: effects of creatine on human bodies
narrative: Relevant: studies of creatine supplementation in people and its effects on any outcome (muscle, exercise performance, cognition, kidney function, aging). Not relevant: creatine kinase used as a lab marker of muscle damage, creatinine as a kidney function test, or animal-only studies.

query: lowering high blood pressure without medication
narrative: Relevant: studies of non-drug ways to lower blood pressure in people with hypertension, such as diet, salt reduction, exercise, weight loss, sleep or stress reduction. Not relevant: trials of blood pressure drugs, or hypertension studies with no intervention.

Relevant: human studies of intermittent fasting, time-restricted eating or alternate-day fasting that report weight, body composition or metabolic outcomes. Not relevant: fasting before surgery or lab tests, or religious fasting studies with no weight or metabolic outcome.

Relevant: human studies of melatonin (supplements or melatonin-receptor drugs) for falling asleep, sleep quality, insomnia or jet lag. Not relevant: melatonin as a biomarker, or melatonin studied for cancer, inflammation or other non-sleep effects.

Relevant: studies reporting adverse effects, safety or tolerability of semaglutide or other GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g. nausea, pancreatitis, gastroparesis, muscle loss). Not relevant: studies that only report effectiveness for weight or blood sugar.

Relevant: studies of preventing kidney or urinary stones from forming or coming back, through diet, fluid intake, medication or risk factor management. Not relevant: surgical or procedural techniques for removing stones.

Relevant: studies of lasting cognitive problems after COVID-19 (memory, concentration, mental fatigue), including causes, prevalence and treatment. Not relevant: acute neurological complications during infection, or long COVID studies with no cognitive outcome.

query: screen time and kids mental health
narrative: Relevant: studies linking screen use, social media or digital device use in children or adolescents to depression, anxiety, sleep, attention or wellbeing. Not relevant: studies of adults only, or screening programs (the word 'screen' in the medical-test sense).
Relevant: studies of vitamin D levels or vitamin D supplementation and depressive symptoms or depressive disorders. Not relevant: vitamin D studies with no mood outcome.

query: treatment for ringing in the ears
narrative: Relevant: studies of treating or managing tinnitus (sound therapy, CBT, devices, drugs, neuromodulation). Not relevant: tinnitus listed only as a side effect, or hearing loss studies that do not address tinnitus.
Relevant: studies of nighttime bedwetting (nocturnal enuresis) in children, including causes, alarms, desmopressin or other treatments. Not relevant: adult urinary incontinence.

query: how well does the shingles vaccine work
narrative: Relevant: studies of herpes zoster vaccine effectiveness, immune response, duration of protection or safety. Not relevant: shingles treatment, or chickenpox (varicella) vaccine studies in children.

Relevant: studies of the link between periodontal disease and cardiovascular disease, including whether treating gum disease affects heart outcomes. Not relevant: gum disease studies with no cardiovascular angle.

Relevant: studies of therapeutic peptides such as BPC-157, TB-500 or thymosin beta-4, or collagen peptides, for healing tendons, ligaments, muscle or other injuries. Not relevant: antimicrobial peptides, peptide hormones like insulin, or peptides used only as biomarkers.

query: SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
narrative: Relevant: clinical or mechanistic studies of SGLT2 inhibitors (e.g. empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) in HFpEF. Not relevant: SGLT2 inhibitor studies in diabetes or reduced ejection fraction only.
